notes:
Passed on the fake backend by python3 -m mhs.driver check (evidence contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level). Model-authored and unreviewed; no hardware backend was run and the wire syntax was not tried on an instrument. The fake is a stateful register map whose start values are placeholders, not a recording and not an upstream simulator (the clone has none). Limits cover frequency, amplitude, phase, DC offset, harmonic, the filter time constant and the X/Y/R offsets; the frequency bound is the SR860 range (0.001 Hz to 500 kHz), so the SR865 (2 MHz) and SR865A (4 MHz) ranges are not accepted. Not exposed: the reference source, external-reference trigger, sensitivity, filter slope, output expand, input mode/coupling/range/ground/impedance, the simultaneous XYRP read, the auto range/scale/phase/offset functions and *RST; no catalogue class binds those actions. The e-stop writes SLVL 0.000000001 (the lowest amplitude the upstream code states) and is a software command, not an independent hardware stop; the driver is R1, so no hardware e-stop is required. gate.digest is the digest the check printed (the report without its clock); check-report.json is regenerated by every gate run and is not part of the package.
